why: What a dev hot swap of the SESSION-OWNING plugin owes every open window. A hot swap destroys the live app instance and creates a successor, and the shell's windows are rebuilt from the session. Between those two points the shell used to keep a live canvas over a session that named the DESTROYED instance, so every retained surface remounted against it: on 26/09/15, :6023, the Flow window's node-graph host mounted 2.3 s after the swap and its first three dispatches — `interactionSelect`, `readLocalInteraction` and the opening-camera `viewport` — were all refused with `no channel for instance 1`, `attachSurface` rejected, and the board stayed blank for the rest of the page. Nothing re-attaches it afterwards: the React surface effect is keyed on `surfaceId` alone, and `window:procedural-main` is the same string on both instances, so the successor session never produces a second mount. The rule is therefore an ORDERING rule, not a retry: a window must never be presented over a retired instance.
liveDefect: ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, `📓️hot-swap-board-remount-2026-09-15.md` §1. Earlier sightings of the same window with different symptoms: `📓️flow-surface-followup-2026-09-15.md` §7 ("the Flow window has no node-graph host at all"), `📓️host-refresh-latency-2026-09-15.md` §3 (the `no channel` ledger, which silenced the errors but did not restore the board).

rules.sessionRetiredBeforeItsInstanceDies: `retire-session` precedes `destroy-instance`: the shell stops naming an instance at the latest instant it is still alive.
rules.canvasLiveOnlyOverALiveSession: No step may leave the canvas presented while the session names a retired instance. This is the whole law; every other rule exists to make it hold.
rules.canvasPresentedAfterTheSuccessor: `present-canvas` follows `establish-session`, because presenting is what mounts the windows and a window mounts against whatever session is current.
rules.oneBoardMountPerSwap: A surface whose React effect is keyed on its `surfaceId` mounts once per presentation. A plan that presents twice pays two mounts and the first one is the wasted one.
rules.reloadBeginsUnpresented: A hot swap of the session-owning plugin first takes the canvas OFF screen (`SET_PLUGIN_STATUS "reloading"`), which is why the measured console shows `node-graph host unmount` before the `hot-swap` line. Every case below therefore starts unpresented; a plugin that owns no session starts presented and stays so.

cases.name: the ordered handover: one board mount, always over a live instance
the measured defect: presenting before the successor exists mounts the board over a corpse, and nothing remounts it
retiring the session first saves the board even when the canvas is presented early
a hot swap of a plugin that owns no session never touches the canvas
